transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Bluecrest Procurement), Lena Torres (Bluecrest Legal), Rajesh Kumar (Bluecrest CTO), Aisha Mbaye (Bluecrest Security)

Summary (auto): Procurement + legal review for Redwood onboarding. Focus on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA commitments, pricing approval and pilot scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Quick agenda: legal redlines, slas, pricing, and next steps for pilot.
[00:17] Samir Patel: Thanks Maya, Samir here from procurement. We're on a tight timeline from finance — need pricing and contract in next two weeks ideally.
[00:30] Lena Torres: Hi all, lena on legal. We'll mainly review DPA and indemnity language, data residency and audit rights.
[00:45] Daniel Ortiz: Hey team, Daniel (SE) — i can cover technical and benchmarking. Quick note: we support hosted, dedicated and private deployments, and can run an on-prem bench if needed.
[01:05] Rajesh Kumar: Hi, Rajesh. For us latency and throughput are main concerns — customer-facing scoring at 100 RPS peak, p95 under 300ms if possible. Also data residency in eu-west for cardholder data.
[01:25] Aisha Mbaye: From security: we need SOC2 report, evidence of KMS integration, audit logs, and SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Great, quick run: MSA + DPA — we usually accept standard redlines, we'll send a consolidated redline doc. On SLAs we offer committed uptime for Dedicated, and hosted has standard 99.5% SLA with optional premium SLA for enterprise. For latency we provide guidance but latency SLAs are tied to deployment and traffic shaping — dedicated gives the most predictable p95.
[02:12] Lena Torres: The indemnity section in your MSA references limited liability caps; we have a carve-out for customer data breaches. Would Redwood consider language change to widen that carve-out?
[02:34] Maya Chen: Understood. We can propose updated indemnity language — i'll Fed that back to legal and propose compromise language, and we can mark it in the redline.
[02:48] Samir Patel: For pricing the CFO wants committed vs pay-as-you-go comparison — reserved capacity discount tiers and an estimate for 6 and 12 month commitments.
[03:05] Daniel Ortiz: We'll share the pricing workbook. Note: Dedicated reserved nodes get 25-40% discount depending on commit. Also batching/kv cache configuration will affect unit cost a lot — we can include expected tokens per second and cost modeling.
[03:28] Rajesh Kumar: Can you share model variants? We need to understand lifecycle and model upgrades, also rollback/fallback behavior during upgrades.
[03:40] Daniel Ortiz: Yes — our model catalog and versioning is part of the platform, we support pinning versions, can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants. We'll include that in the technical annex.
[04:05] Aisha Mbaye: Also compliance: can you support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) in private deployment? And what about audit logs retention?
[04:18] Maya Chen: Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM, retention configurable as an add-on. We'll include SOC2 and compliance attachments.
[04:35] Lena Torres: On data residency — can you guarantee that EU data remains in eu-west for hosted offering?
[04:47] Maya Chen: Yes, region pinning is available. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll call that out in the redline and SOW.
[05:05] Samir Patel: About onboarding — what's typical duration for a pilot and what deliverables should we expect?
[05:18] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya (CSM). Typical pilot 30-60 days: setup, ingestion/connection, 2-3 week benchmark window, quality checks, and handoff. We provide runbooks, onboarding tasks, and a weekly cadence.
[05:39] Samir Patel: Ok good. For procurement we need: PO process, invoice cadence, and any procurement-specific clauses like SLA credits.
[05:50] Maya Chen: We'll include billing terms and invoice cadence in the pricing workbook. SLA credits formula is in the SLA attachment; we can propose language acceptable to finance.
[06:05] Lena Torres: Back to the DPA — can you confirm subprocessors list and notification process for data breaches?
[06:17] Maya Chen: We'll provide a current subprocessors list and our incident response timeline. We notify within defined windows and will include that in the DPA.
[06:30] Rajesh Kumar: For the benchmark, we want to run two profiles: steady throughput at 100 RPS and spike test up to 500 RPS for 1 minute. Also tensor quantized models if possible — what's supported?
[06:47] Daniel Ortiz: We support quantized variants and model selection per workload. For spike handling we'll propose burst capacity options on Dedicated; hosted has soft limits but we can configure burst windows. We'll include the benchmark profile in the template.
[07:10] Samir Patel: Legal typically needs redline within 5 business days; procurement needs pricing and PO info within the same window.
[07:22] Maya Chen: We'll aim to send the MSA/DPA consolidated redline by Friday (2026-05-14) and the pricing workbook and pilot plan by Wednesday (2026-05-13).
[07:40] Lena Torres: One more item — indemnity and liability caps tied to fees, we usually ask for a cap of 3x fees or a defined carve-out, any flexibility?
[07:55] Maya Chen: I can't finalize here but we'll propose language tradeoffs. Often we discuss carve-outs for willful misconduct and data breaches; we'll present options in the redline so you can share with counsel.
[08:10] Aisha Mbaye: On encryption in transit at rest — do you support customer-managed keys for hosted offering or only for Private?
[08:20] Daniel Ortiz: Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in some regions; full HSM customer control is available in Private deployments. We'll clarify in doc.
[08:35] Samir Patel: Pricing question: are there any setup fees or professional services for onboarding?
[08:45] Priya Nair: There can be a one-time onboarding fee for enterprise integrations (SSO, KMS, custom VPC peering). We'll list optional professional services and estimates in the pricing workbook.
[09:02] Lena Torres: We'll want to review the DPA's audit rights and breach notification timeline. Also certificate of compliance (SOC2) — please attach last 12 months report.
[09:15] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and ISO where available.
[09:25] Rajesh Kumar: On routing/fallback — if a model version is failing, can Redwood route to a lower-cost variant automatically? Concerns about quiet failures affecting production.
[09:38] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants is supported; we can configure health checks and auto-fallback policies. We'll include examples in the technical annex.
[10:00] Samir Patel: For procurement approval, the CFO needs estimated monthly burn for production and pilot. Can you provide a 3-scenario estimate? (pilot, 6mo reserved, 12mo reserved)
[10:12] Daniel Ortiz: We'll produce scenario modeling with token estimates and cost per 1k tokens, with reserved node discounts.
[10:25] Maya Chen: Alright, i want to recap next steps — we'll send: 1) consolidated MSA/DPA redline, 2) pricing workbook with scenarios and discount tiers, 3) pilot plan + benchmark template, 4) security artifacts (SOC2, subprocessors, KMS details), and 5) onboarding runbook.
[10:45] Lena Torres: Sounds good. Expect legal redline by 2026-05-20 from us.
[10:55] Samir Patel: Procurement will review pricing and PO flow, i'll confirm deadlines with finance and get back.
[11:05] Maya Chen: Great — any final questions?
[11:12] Aisha Mbaye: Quick one: is there a standard SLA credit formula? We need how credits are calculated and applied to invoices.
[11:22] Maya Chen: Yes it's percentage of monthly fees pro-rated to downtime windows; we'll attach the SLA schedule.
[11:35] Rajesh Kumar: Ok thanks, we'll await the documents and schedule the bench session.
[11:45] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the documents by the dates noted.
[11:52] [END]
